Ebbinghaus veut mesurer la mémoire comme: Ebbinghaus wants to measure memory the way a physicist measures heat. So that the meaning of words won't help him, he invents 2,300 nonsense syllables, like DAX or BOK, and learns them himself in lists, to the beat of a metronome. He records how many repetitions he needs to relearn a list after a few minutes, hours or days. Result: forgetting is very fast at first, then slows down; this is the forgetting curve. He also shows that reviews spaced out over time are far more effective than massed reviews. For years, he was the only subject of his experiments.

He describes how intelligence is built before language, through action: the infant first repeats reflexes, then gestures that produce an amusing effect, then invents new means to reach a goal. Around eight months, object permanence appears: a toy hidden under a sheet still exists. For Piaget, the child is not a miniature adult: they think differently, in successive stages.
